Subject: Retainer apportionment & partial-pay routing for BrightGrid pilot

Hi Elena / Marco,

Thanks again for the productive kickoff yesterday. As we move toward onboarding BrightGrid for the pilot, finance asked for a clear apportionment approach for the initial retainer and subsequent monthly invoices so your internal cost centers can be billed to the appropriate legal entities.

Quick ask: can you confirm the entities you want us to split the retainer across and whether BrightGrid requires separate invoices per legal entity or a single invoice with internal chargebacks?

What we propose (draft):
- Collect a single retainer from BrightGrid (PO 7892) but issue split invoice lines mapped to three BrightGrid legal entities (BG-US, BG-EU, BG-UK).
- Send one consolidated invoice PDF to your AP inbox, with a summary page that lists payment routing (wiring instructions) per entity + GL codes.
- For EU/UK lines where VAT reverse-charge may apply, we will mark the line with the appropriate tax tag and include your VAT registration numbers in the invoice metadata.

If that approach works, please attach the entity list (legal name, VAT/Tax ID, remit instructions, desired PO allocation percentages) and indicate whether you prefer:
A) Single remittance from BrightGrid and we sweep & route internally to entities (Redwood handles internal allocation), or
B) BrightGrid sends split remittances to each legal entity directly.

Action: please confirm A or B and attach the entity details. If helpful, I can run this by our finance team and propose a sample invoice layout.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0124

Jordan / Elena / team —

Thanks for the details. Finance and Legal reviewed and agree with option A (Redwood collects single payment and performs the internal apportion). Summary of the final approach and operational checklist below:

1) Invoice format and delivery
- Redwood will issue a consolidated invoice PDF to finance@brightgrid.io.
- The PDF will include a first summary page with total retainer amount and a clear payment routing table listing the three BrightGrid entities, allocation percentages, remit instructions, and the per-entity GL codes.
- Each invoice line will include a custom field (EntityCode) that BrightGrid can map on import.

2) Tax/VAT handling
- For BG-EU lines, Redwood will include the reverse-charge note: "VAT reversed under Article 44/196 EU & Customer liable for local VAT" and will include BG-EU VAT ID (DE123456789).
- For BG-UK lines, we will leave VAT at 0% where you provide a valid UK VAT number prior to invoicing; otherwise we will apply local VAT and follow up. Karthik: legal sign-off comment attached accepted.

3) Intercompany / sweep steps
- Redwood will accept the single remittance to Redwood US bank account. We will perform an internal sweep to remit the apportioned amounts to Redwood Europe/UK entities per configured wires. Those intercompany transfers will be processed within 7 business days of posting.
- Avery will provide the GL mapping and memo line format: "BG-PO7892 / RDW-INV-[INVNUM] / EntityCode=[ENTITYCODE]"

4) Controls & reconciliation
- We'll attach a machine-readable CSV export with the invoice (line-level allocations + entity GL code + tax tags) so BrightGrid can auto-import for reconciliation.
- If BrightGrid prefers, we can also provide separate per-entity PDF stubs as supporting docs in the invoice package.

5) Next steps / actions
- Jordan: please confirm with BrightGrid that option A is accepted (they already said yes).
- Elena: please confirm BG-UK VAT number before EOW so we can invoice without UK VAT.
- Karthik: we accept the reverse-charge wording as-is.
- Avery: please share the final GL mapping file by EOD 9/2 so we include the correct codes in the invoice metadata.

DocuSign: Elena, we will send a short retainer amendment to reflect the apportionment workflow and intercompany sweep. Please sign to confirm acceptance. Link: https://app.docusign.com/retainer-amendment/BG-7892

Kimberly Park
